08 Standards, regulatory pathway and ethics

BMED Chapter 11 (standards), Chapter 12 (regulatory requirements: FDA classification, pathways, design controls), Chapter 13 (ethics), and 6.3.1 / 6.3.4 (regulatory and standards screening).

1. Standards that apply to the selected concept (A)

StandardScopeHow this design addresses itGap before clinical use
IEC 60601-1-8 Alarm systemsAlarm priorities, colours, technical vs physiological alarmsThree priorities plus technical SIGNAL CHECK; colour plus shape; persistence and hysteresis; fixed banner positionAudible signals, alarm silencing/pausing, and alarm logging belong to the host monitor
IEC 62304 Medical device software life cycleSoftware development, SOUP, risk-based classSOUP list (doc 05 §4); frozen, checksum-verified model (FMEA R-13); scripted verification; risk controls traced to testsLikely software safety class C (failure could contribute to serious injury). Needs a formal SDP, unit-level verification records and configuration management
ISO 14971 Risk managementHazard analysis, risk evaluation and controlFMEA (doc 06), 13 risks, controls verified by measurement, risk–benefit statementPost-market surveillance plan; field data for probabilities
IEC 62366-1 Usability engineeringUse specification, formative and summative evaluationUse specification (doc 06 §1.1), formative heuristic evaluationSummative evaluation with users (doc 07 §8, V3)
ISO 13485 Quality management systemDesign controls, DHFThis DHF follows the design-control structure (inputs, outputs, verification, reviews)A QMS would be needed by any manufacturer
ISO 81060-2 Non-invasive sphygmomanometers, clinical validationAccuracy of BP measurement (mean error ≤ 5 mmHg, SD ≤ 8 mmHg)Used as the accuracy reference for SPEC-01. A measures against an arterial line; it does not claim to be a BP measurement deviceWould apply in full to any non-invasive claim (Concept B)
IEEE 11073 / HL7 FHIR device data exchangeMonitor connectivityNot implemented (replay prototype)Needed for live data
FDA cybersecurity guidance (2023)Premarket cybersecurityLocalhost-only server, input-size limits, path-traversal protection, no external callsThreat model, SBOM, penetration test

2. Regulatory classification and pathway (United States)

Is it a device? The FDA's 2022 Clinical Decision Support guidance says that software which acquires, processes or analyses a medical signal (for example ECG or arterial waveforms) does not meet the non-device CDS criteria. All three concepts process physiological waveforms, so all three are devices, including Concept C.

Concept AConcept BConcept C
Likely classIIIIII (possibly lower risk within II)
Predicate / product codeHypotension Prediction Index: De Novo DEN160044, regulation 21 CFR 870.2210 (adjunctive predictive cardiovascular indicator)Same regulation, but non-invasive pressure estimation adds ISO 81060-2 accuracy claims870.2210 or a physiological-data review classification
Pathway510(k) with HPI as predicate (substantial equivalence: same intended use, predictive indicator of hypotension; different technology → performance data)510(k) or De Novo with new clinical data; current evidence fails the needed accuracy510(k)
Evidence neededRetrospective + prospective performance study; software documentation (IEC 62304 class C); human factorsAll of A's, plus ISO 81060-2 clinical validationSoftware documentation; performance of the retrospective analysis
Regulatory risk (selection criterion C8)MediumHighLower

Labelling consequence of this project's evidence. The Version 5 intended-use statement (Version 5/docs/samd/intended_use.md) describes the model as processing non-invasive ECG + PPG data, indicated "when continuous invasive arterial line monitoring is either unavailable, contraindicated, or awaiting placement". The verification in this project does not support that claim. On held-out real patients the ECG + PPG configuration reached AUROC 0.59 and MAE 12.6 mmHg, and under-alerted during 100% of critical-hypotension time in simulation. The intended use should be revised to match Concept A:

Adjunctive decision support for adult patients in the operating room or ICU with an indwelling arterial line, providing a 15-second forecast of mean arterial pressure, an alert when the forecast indicates hypotension, and a display of the haemodynamic response after clinician-recorded interventions. Not for use as the sole basis for diagnosis or treatment. Not a replacement for the arterial-line pressure display or its alarms.

The Version 5 statement also says the device allows "proactive clinical intervention, such as the administration of vasopressors or fluid resuscitation". This app deliberately reports observations and trends only (SPEC-14), so that it does not suggest a therapy.

3. Ethics (BMED Chapter 13)

PrincipleConcern in this projectDesign response
Non-maleficenceFalse reassurance is the most harmful failure (H-09)Fail-safe design: RC-08 and RC-10 ensure that losing information can never lower an alarm; SPEC-15 makes this a must-meet requirement
BeneficenceAn alert that adds noise without benefit wastes attentionBenefits measured honestly against a fair datum, including where the design does not beat current practice (persistence benchmark, lead time)
Autonomy / clinician authorityAutomation bias; the software could appear to decideDecision support only; every output explains its basis; no treatment recommendations (verified by scan, 0 found)
JusticeConcept B was motivated by lower-resource settingsB was not deployed because a tool that is wrong more often in under-resourced settings would widen, not close, the gap. Kept as a research goal
Honesty in reportingPressure to present a winning conceptSelection weaknesses reported: C wins 66% of random weightings; A's lead time is seconds; A fails SPEC-04 and 08
Data privacyPatient waveformsOnly de-identified public data (VitalDB) and simulation; server binds to localhost; no telemetry
Equity of dataVitalDB is one surgical centre in KoreaStated as a threat to validity; validation plan includes other cohorts
Conflicts of interestNone declared–

4. Intellectual property (BMED 6.3.5)

Possibly novel: combining a physics-informed (Windkessel-constrained) forecaster with a fail-safe alarm layer (confidence-capped priority, evidence-ranked hold, measured-pressure floor). The HPI patent family (Edwards Lifesciences) would need a freedom-to-operate review before commercialisation. No filing is planned for this academic project.
